description: Same-history delayed voter replies consumed by verification after a higher-term leader commits.

harness.description: Real three-voter prefix; hold four positive old replies before partition; public timeout reload and real new election/Apply; then invoke old VerifyLeader and release held replies. Independently observe current-leader control and locked FSM command presence.
semantic_changes: Transport wrapper withholds first real reply from each old peer sender loop and parks subsequent old calls; no response fields are changed.
Disable optional pipeline support using supported error fallback.
Use public Disconnect and ReloadConfig to establish a bounded legal network/scheduling history.
Observe future.Error, public State/CurrentTerm, persisted configuration and locked MockFSM command presence. No target protocol state is assigned.

legality.derivation: BootstrapCluster/NewRaft start three actual voters. Old leader wins, Apply(prefix).Error returns nil, persisted config is read and compared to public membership, and each locked MockFSM contains prefix. Once active, wrapper reserves the first ordinary and heartbeat call per peer; each calls InmemTransport and captures actual response before withholding return to its sender. After four positive term-matching replies exist, links old<->peers are disconnected; peers remain connected to each other. Public ReloadConfig lowers only peer election/heartbeat timeouts after validation. A peer must become Leader at a strictly higher term and complete Apply(new-leader-command), whose FSM presence is verified, before any VerifyLeader call. All subsequent old outbound append/heartbeat calls park until cleanup and then return a transport-unavailable error; no new response is fabricated. Higher-term incoming paths to old are unavailable through explicit partition. Active old lease may demote naturally. Held replies release only after old verification enqueue. New leader control runs in the same cluster afterwards, with independent op identity. Gate release/park cleanup and Shutdown bound all waits.
legality.applicability: Non-Byzantine delayed response delivery and bidirectional partition; membership unchanged. Wrapper delay begins after receiver production and before caller return, modeling delayed delivery without editing response fields. Per-node timeout settings and reload are accepted by target API; safety result is scoped to those values. No direct term, role, vote, commit index or notification mutation.
unresolved: Peer timeout reload changes scheduling configuration, not voter membership. Equal-timeout deployments are outside this execution.
Any missed setup transition or observation deadline leaves no matched result rather than providing a passing safety observation.
alternatives: Old lease expiration and negative/higher-term responses are valid rejection mechanisms; lease runs, but the selected transport partition delays those responses.
Ordinary replication and heartbeat are both present; disabling optional pipelines follows the existing supported fallback.

grounding.derivation: The implication is superseded-at-admission => success=false. Superseded is independently selected from target ID versus the observed newer leader ID after actual higher-term election and successful Apply completed. The driver validates newTerm > captured oldTerm. Four real positive old-term replies are captured before the split; the future is invoked after new-write completion, and held replies are released afterwards. No timeout is encoded as violation or success. The current-leader control has antecedent false and records its actual result, demonstrating a permitted path without requiring its success as part of the safety implication.
grounding.applicability: Fixed three voters, real startup/elections/committed prefix, finite selective response delays and isolation. Lease timers remain active. Old node uses 900 ms lease; peers use 50 ms leases and are reloaded through the public API to 80 ms election/heartbeat after reply capture. The API validates each setting; no equal-timeout requirement is stated in acquired configuration documentation.
unresolved: Exact callback that drains old verification (ordinary append versus heartbeat) is not isolated.
The observed command-presence field is diagnostic; the primary oracle checks successful authority verification after an independently established prior transition.
alternatives: If lease expires or a higher-term/negative reply reaches the old node first, it may correctly fail verification; such outcomes must remain visible.
An in-flight success from before admission alone proves no violation unless later authority was independently established before invocation.

observable_properties.description: A verification invoked on the superseded node after a different higher-term leader completed its write must not return success. The antecedent is established independently by actual prior election/write and target identity, not by absence of connectivity or expected outcome.

uncertainties: This checks the VerifyLeader authority contract; it does not establish divergent committed logs or overall consensus failure.
Diagnostic old FSM omission of the newer completed command is an observed stale-data consequence at this endpoint, not a universal read-protocol theorem.
The wrapper delays transport completion after actual reply production; it is not a real TCP packet-loss implementation.
Current-leader control shares the cluster transition but is a separate future; histories and identities are not merged.
